fields.value: The recognition modules mostly detected the targeted cues in preliminary tests. Back-channel detection correctly identified 9, 10, and 10 instances for the three subjects; nod detection was mostly successful, with more false negatives for one participant whose nods were slighter. No statistical significance tests were reported.

fields.value: The authors frame gaze and body direction as attention directions and as cues of recipiency, which can be exaggerated by the telepresence robot.

quotes.text: Gaze directions and body directions belong to attention directions.
We called these cues as cues of recipiency.

fields.value: Cues of recipiency are non-verbal cues used to obtain the address; they indicate that the listener is receiving and interested.

fields.value: Attention directions and response cues help a remote participant become the addressee, a step toward becoming the next speaker and taking a turn.

quotes.text: Therefore, becoming addressee is previous step to become speaker and take turns.

fields.value: Kinect provides skeletal tracking, facial tracking, and sound pressure. Software detects speaking to switch between speaker and recipient modes; recipient mode detects back-channels, attention time, and nods, then generates exaggerated motion commands for the robot.

quotes.text: According to the result of speaking recognition, the system switched the expression modes, which are speaker mode and recipient mode.
Then, based on these cues, the system generated exaggerated motion.
When the attention time was more than 3 seconds, the module generated the motion that got the robot to turn the body to the attended participant.

fields.value: A KHR-3HV desktop-sized humanoid robot with two 4-DOF arms, a 2-DOF waist, a 3-DOF neck, and a small display for the remote operator’s face.

quotes.text: We employed KHR-3HV that is a desktop sized humanoid robot by Kondo Kagaku Company as the robot ’s platform.
Accordingly, the robot had two 4 DOF arms which enables various kinds of hand gestures.
It also had a 2 DOF waist, which allows leaning forwarding motions and changing body directions.
For expressing head motions and looking directions, it had a 3 DOF neck.

fields.value: The paper presents a telepresence robot that detects a remote participant’s attention directions, nods, and back-channels and exaggerates them as robot motions to help the participant become an addressee and take turns in multiparty teleconferences. Preliminary tests evaluated cue-recognition modules, but the effect on multiparty interaction was left for future work.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ4; RQ5; RQ6 — The paper describes gaze and body direction as attention-direction cues of recipiency, explains their intended role in addressee selection and turn-taking, and details the sensing and robot implementation. It describes the robot embodiment and its expressive capabilities, but does not test embodiment effects or interaction outcomes.
